title: [Inductor] Inductor is slower than vLLM XPU fused kernels for small MXFP8 quantization input shapes
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

On Intel XPU, the current `torch.compile` + Inductor path is slower than the vLLM XPU fused kernel baseline for MXFP8 quantization patterns with small input shapes.

This matters for LLM serving because decode / small-batch phases often run these quantization patterns on small input tensors. In the reproducer, the main dynamic dimension is `M`, the first dimension of the input tensor, e.g. `x.shape == [M, K]`. In this latency-dominated regime, Inductor appears to have higher fixed overhead than the vLLM XPU fused kernels.

## What is compared

This issue uses three representative model input shapes:

- Llama-3.1-70B
- Qwen3-32B
- Qwen3-30B-A3B

The reproducer compares two implementations of the same MXFP8 quantization patterns:

1. **Inductor**: decomposed torch ops compiled with `torch.compile(backend="inductor")`.
2. **vLLM XPU fused baseline**: custom ops from `vllm_xpu_kernels._C`, such as `rms_norm`, `fused_add_rms_norm`, `silu_and_mul`, and `per_token_group_fp8_quant`.

The main metric is:

```text
Inductor/fused = compiled_ms / fused_ms
```

`Inductor/fused > 1` means Inductor is slower than the vLLM fused baseline.

## Observed result

Existing XPU benchmark data plus a targeted rerun for `M=128,256` show the small-shape gap and the crossover point:

| M in input shape `[M, K]` | Cases | Median Inductor/fused | Inductor faster | Inductor slower |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 12 | 1.373984 | 0/12 | 12/12 |
| 8 | 12 | 1.426034 | 0/12 | 12/12 |
| 16 | 12 | 1.387500 | 0/12 | 12/12 |
| 64 | 12 | 1.370652 | 2/12 | 10/12 |
| 128 | 12 | 1.187826 | 3/12 | 9/12 |
| 256 | 12 | 0.768078 | 9/12 | 3/12 |
| 1024 | 12 | 0.420336 | 11/12 | 1/12 |

Each row aggregates 3 model input shapes × 4 MXFP8 quantization patterns = 12 cases.

The issue is concentrated in the small-shape regime: for `M = 1, 8, 16`, all measured cases are slower than the vLLM XPU fused baseline; at `M = 64` and `M = 128`, most cases are still slower. By `M = 256`, Inductor becomes faster in most cases, and by `M = 1024` it is clearly faster for almost all cases.

The raw rows are included in `observed_3models_rows.csv`; the summary table above is in `observed_3models_summary.csv`.

## Expected behavior

For small MXFP8 quantization input shapes, Inductor should be competitive with the vLLM XPU fused kernel baseline, or at least avoid a consistent ~1.3x median slowdown.

## Reproducer

[repro_3models_mxfp8_inductor_vs_fused_xpu.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28390603/repro_3models_mxfp8_inductor_vs_fused_xpu.py)

Run inside an existing vLLM nightly / `vllm-xpu-kernels` environment on XPU:

```bash
python repro_3models_mxfp8_inductor_vs_fused_xpu.py \
  --m-sizes 1 8 16 64 128 256 1024 \
  --warmup 20 \
  --repeat 200 \
  --csv three_models_mxfp8_inductor_vs_fused.csv
```

The script prints environment provenance (`torch.__version__`, `torch.version.git_version`, `torch.__file__`, and XPU device name) and writes:

```text
config,pattern,M,compiled_ms,fused_ms,inductor_over_fused
```

## Environment used for the observed data

- Device: Intel XPU / BMG-class device (B60)
- PyTorch nightly XPU wheel: observed artifact recorded `torch 2.13.0.dev20260527+xpu`, git `7723df38831f748f0091beb914c86c6182334c27`
- vLLM XPU kernels environment: vLLM nightly / `vllm_xpu_kernels` installed, fused baseline available via `vllm_xpu_kernels._C`

## Scope

This issue is only about the latency gap for small MXFP8 quantization input shapes. The same benchmark shows Inductor can perform well on larger shapes; this issue is not claiming Inductor is generally slower.

title: [OOB][Perf] aten::native_batch_norm performance gap on B580 (13 models affected)
body:
## Summary

`aten::native_batch_norm` is the top 4 op priority on B580 for XPU performance improvement in OOB 300 eager inference (fp16). The gap is significantly larger on B580 than G31, suggesting a platform-specific kernel issue.

## Data (from roofline profiling, 154 models, fp16 inference)

| Platform | Geomean R Delta | Models Affected | Total Saving (ms) |
|----------|------:|------:|------:|
| B580 | +0.0049 | 13 | 6,168 |
| G31 (B70) | +0.0012 | 10 | 145 |

Current fleet geomean R: B580=0.644, G31=0.675, 4080S=0.683.
## Note

The B580 total saving (6,168 ms) is 42x larger than G31 (145 ms) despite fewer affected models. This strongly suggests a B580-specific performance issue with the batch_norm kernel — likely related to occupancy, vectorization, or memory access patterns on BMG architecture.

Batch norm is a memory-bound op (vector engine). The roofline projects it at bytes/BW, so a gap means the kernel is not achieving peak bandwidth on B580.

## Hardware

- B580: 93 TFLOPS fp16, 410 GB/s
- G31 (B70): 154 TFLOPS fp16, 532 GB/s
- 4080S: 100.96 TFLOPS fp16, 716.8 GB/s

title: [OOB][Perf] aten::clone unnecessary memory copies on XPU (18 models affected)
body:
## Summary

`aten::clone` is the top 3 op priority on B580 and top 5 on G31 for XPU performance improvement in OOB 300 eager inference (fp16). Clone creates unnecessary memory copies that inflate T2 relative to CUDA. This could indicate missing in-place optimizations or suboptimal memory format handling on XPU.

## Data (from roofline profiling, 154 models, fp16 inference)

Current fleet geomean R: B580=0.644, G31=0.675, 4080S=0.683.

title: [BMG] PyTorch 2.12 performance cases where inductor is slower than eager (speedup < 1)
body:
## Summary

BMG PyTorch 2.12 release performance results contain multiple cases where inductor is slower than eager (`speedup < 1`).

These are PyTorch 2.12 release performance results collected from the raw performance artifacts:

- Platform: BMG (Battlemage)
- PyTorch: `torch 2.12.0+xpu`
- Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, `intel-opencl-icd 26.05.37020.3`, `libze-dev 1.27.0`, `intel-opencl-rt 2025.3.2`, `oneMKL 2025.3.1`

## Representative Cases

The rows below come directly from the raw PyTorch 2.12 performance CSVs and show `speedup < 1`, which means inductor is slower than eager on the same workload.

| suite | dtype | mode | model | batch_size | speedup | source csv |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| huggingface | bfloat16 | inference | `ElectraForQuestionAnswering` | 128 | 0.662224 | `huggingface/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | bfloat16 | inference | `BertForQuestionAnswering` | 32 | 0.732601 | `huggingface/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | bfloat16 | inference | `BartForConditionalGeneration` | 4 | 0.741895 | `huggingface/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | bfloat16 | inference | `MBartForConditionalGeneration` | 4 | 0.723328 | `huggingface/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | bfloat16 | inference | `PLBartForConditionalGeneration` | 8 | 0.829213 | `huggingface/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | amp_bf16 | inference | `BertForQuestionAnswering` | 32 | 0.893284 | `huggingface/amp_bf16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-amp_bf16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | float16 | inference | `ElectraForQuestionAnswering` | 128 | 0.646220 | `huggingface/float16/inference/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-float16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| huggingface | bfloat16 | training | `OPTForCausalLM` | 2 | 0.876858 | `huggingface/bfloat16/training/performance/inductor-results-huggingface-bfloat16-training-xpu-performance.csv` |
| torchbench | bfloat16 | inference | `lennard_jones` | 1000 | 0.671808 | `torchbench/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-torchbench-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| torchbench | bfloat16 | inference | `maml` | 1 | 0.664822 | `torchbench/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-torchbench-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |
| torchbench | bfloat16 | inference | `soft_actor_critic` | 256 | 0.865522 | `torchbench/bfloat16/inference/performance/inductor-results-torchbench-bfloat16-inference-xpu-performance.csv` |

There are additional PyTorch 2.12 rows with the same pattern outside this representative subset.

## Notes

- The pattern is concentrated in inference workloads, especially HuggingFace QA/seq2seq style models and several TorchBench models.
- These rows were taken from the raw perf artifacts rather than the generated comparison CSV, because the goal here is to flag inductor-vs-eager gaps directly in the PyTorch 2.12 release results.

## Ask

Please review these BMG PyTorch 2.12 cases and track the inductor performance gaps where eager is still faster than inductor.

title: XPU/XCCL all_gather + torch.xpu.empty_cache leaks device-global memory
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

On Intel XPU with XCCL, repeated PyTorch distributed allgather operations followed by deleting tensors and calling `torch.xpu.empty_cache()` leak device global memory. PyTorch allocator stats return to the expected value, but `torch.xpu.mem_get_info()` free memory drops every iteration until XPU OOM.

## Minimal Repro

To reproduce ([see the repro here in our CI/CD for more details](https://github.com/argonne-lcf/frameworks-sdk/tree/main/tests/single_node/functionality/torch-xpu-ops/allgather_hidden_temp_memleak)):
```
module load frameworks
mkdir -p allgather_hidden_temp_memleak
curl -L https://github.com/argonne-lcf/frameworks-sdk/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz |
  tar -xz -C allgather_hidden_temp_memleak --strip-components=6 \
  --wildcards '*/tests/single_node/functionality/torch-xpu-ops/allgather_hidden_temp_memleak/*'

./allgather_hidden_temp_memleak/run_repros.sh

#or if no mpiexec
./allgather_hidden_temp_memleak/run_repros_torchrun.sh
```
You might need to set any relevant oneCCL env vars depending on your test system.

## Expected 

After tensors are deleted and `torch.xpu.empty_cache()` runs, device global free memory should return to a stable baseline.

## Actual

For `world_size=2`, `TENSOR_SIZE=100000000`, `bf16`, list `dist.all_gather` loses `0.373 GiB` per iteration, exactly matching the hidden flattened output temp size.

```text
summary | mode=list_hidden_temp expected_temp=0.373GiB observed_drop_per_iter=0.373GiB
summary | mode=into_persistent expected_temp=0.373GiB observed_drop_per_iter=0.000GiB
summary | mode=explicit_temp expected_temp=0.373GiB observed_drop_per_iter=0.373GiB
summary | mode=temp_no_collective expected_temp=0.373GiB observed_drop_per_iter=0.000GiB
```

## Suspected Code

I'm pretty sure the bug is happening here: https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/blob/main/src/xccl/ProcessGroupXCCL.cpp#L1644-L1669

In the `torch-xpu-ops/src/xccl/ProcessGroupXCCL.cpp`, list all-gather path:

```cpp
at::Tensor outputFlattened = newLikeFlat(outputTensors_);
xccl::onecclAllGather(input, outputFlattened, comm, xcclStream, stream);
outputTensors_[j].copy_(outputFlattened[j], true);
```

The issue appears when a tensor that participated in XCCL all-gather is later released to Level Zero via `torch.xpu.empty_cache()`.

## Additional Notes

This does not reproduce with allocation/free/`empty_cache()` alone, and I tried a pure oneCCL/SYCL malloc/free/allgather test which also never failed. The failing API surface is PyTorch ProcessGroupXCCL plus PyTorch XPU allocator lifetime.

### Versions

N/A

title: [Triton 3.7.1] Inductor inference latency regression on PVC — 50 models affected (10–20x slower)
body:
## Summary

Triton 3.7.1 introduces severe inductor latency regressions on **PVC (Ponte Vecchio)** for **inference-only** workloads. 50 model/dtype/mode combinations are affected, with inductor latency increasing **10–20x** compared to Triton 3.7.0 baseline.

**Training workloads are unaffected.** Eager latency is stable between target and baseline, confirming this is a Triton compilation/codegen issue, not an environment problem.

## Environment

| Component | Target | Baseline |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Triton | 3.7.1 (`2bafaf80`) | 3.7.1 (`21033c4e2be`) |
| PyTorch | torch 2.12.0+xpu (nightly) | torch 2.12.0+xpu (nightly) |
| Platform | PVC (Data Center Max) | PVC (Data Center Max) |

## Affected Models

All are **inference mode** across multiple dtypes (amp_bf16, amp_fp16, bfloat16, float16).
Ratio = baseline_latency / target_latency (values < 1.0 mean target is slower):

| Model | Suite | Inductor Ratio | Eager Ratio |
|-------|-------|----------------|-------------|
| fbnetc_100 | timm_models | **0.054x** | 1.00x |
| ghostnet_100 | timm_models | **0.062x** | 1.00x |
| mnasnet_100 | timm_models | **0.055x** | 1.00x |
| gluon_inception_v3 | timm_models | **0.066x** | 1.03x |
| inception_v3 | timm_models | **0.065x** | 1.03x |
| res2net50_14w_8s | timm_models | **0.063x** | 1.00x |
| resnest101e | timm_models | **0.065x** | 1.00x |
| timm_resnest | torchbench | **0.065x** | 1.01x |
| botnet26t_256 | timm_models | **0.062x** | 1.00x |
| resnet152 | torchbench | **0.069x** | 1.00x |
| resnet50 | torchbench | **0.063x** | 1.00x |
| resnext50_32x4d | torchbench | **0.069x** | 1.00x |
| densenet121 | torchbench | **0.079x** | 1.00x |
| mobilenet_v2 | torchbench | **0.051x** | 1.00x |
| mobilenetv2_100 | timm_models | **0.050x** | 1.00x |
| mnasnet1_0 | torchbench | **0.057x** | 1.00x |
| spnasnet_100 | timm_models | **0.055x** | 1.00x |

## Verification

- **Eager latency ratio is ~1.0x** for all affected models, confirming the test environment is consistent.
- **Training mode is unaffected** — same models in training show inductor latency ratio within 0.97–1.03x.
- Results reproduced on rerun.

## Observations

- All affected architectures use **depthwise separable convolutions** or **mobile-style inverted residual blocks** (MobileNet family, EfficientNet family, ResNeSt, GhostNet).
- The regression appears to be in Triton kernel codegen or scheduling for these specific graph patterns during inference.
- The 10-20x regression suggests compilation is falling back to a suboptimal code path or generating excessive kernel launches.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
docker run -it -e TZ=Aisa/Shanghai --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \
    --privileged --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-24.04-lts2:2523.40 bash

# setup python
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | env UV_INSTALL_DIR="/usr/local/bin" sh
uv venv myvenv --python 3.12 --clear
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip numpy 'setuptools<81' wheel

# install pytorch nightly xpu wheel
uv pip install torch torchaudio torchvision --pre --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu

# prepare pytorch source
pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

# install deps
uv pip install pip pandas psutil scipy requests
uv pip install -U numpy==1.26.4 accelerate
uv pip install -r .ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/huggingface-requirements.txt
uv pip install timm

# sync model list
rm -rf torch torch-xpu-ops
git clone https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops
rsync -avz ./torch-xpu-ops/.ci/benchmarks/ ./benchmarks/dynamo/

git clone https://github.com/pytorch/benchmark tmp-benchmark
cd tmp-benchmark
python install.py --continue_on_fail
cd ..

# uninstall the triton and install new from https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/25853155119?pr=182438

# run affected models (inference)
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --bfloat16 \
  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 \
  --disable-cudagraphs --only resnet50

python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py -d xpu --performance --bfloat16 \
  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 \
  --disable-cudagraphs --only mobilenetv2_100
```

## Workflow Runs

- Target: https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/actions/runs/25921168232
- Baseline: https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/actions/runs/25737207406

## Expected Behavior

Inductor latency should be comparable to or better than baseline for inference workloads (ratio ~1.0x).

title: XPU AOTInductor package fails on complex RoPE-style computation while equivalent real cos/sin implementation passes
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

AOTInductor package execution fails on XPU for a small module that applies rotary embeddings through complex tensors (`torch.polar`, `torch.view_as_complex`, complex multiply, `torch.view_as_real`). The mathematically equivalent real-valued `cos/sin` implementation passes on the same device and through the same AOTInductor package flow.

The failure message includes `AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`, but the repro is running on XPU tensors and `torch.version.cuda=None`. This looks like an internal fallback/proxy/shim issue in the XPU AOTInductor complex operator path rather than user code moving tensors to CUDA.

## Environment

```text
torch=2.13.0.dev20260519+xpu
torch.version.cuda=None
torch.version.xpu=20250302
device=xpu
```

Device available in the repro environment:

```text
Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Minimal Repro

Save this as `repro_aot_complex_rope_xpu.py` and run:

```bash
python repro_aot_complex_rope_xpu.py --device xpu
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
import argparse
import os
import tempfile
import traceback

import torch
from torch._inductor.package import load_package


class ComplexRope(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, seq_len=8, dim=16):
        super().__init__()
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len)
        inv_freq = 1.0 / torch.pow(10000, torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float().div(dim))
        angles = torch.outer(positions, inv_freq)
        self.freqs = torch.polar(torch.ones_like(angles), angles)

    def forward(self, x):
        x_complex = torch.view_as_complex(x.float().reshape(*x.shape[:-1], -1, 2))
        out = torch.view_as_real(x_complex * self.freqs.to(x.device).unsqueeze(1)).flatten(3)
        return out.type_as(x)


class RealRope(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, seq_len=8, dim=16):
        super().__init__()
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len)
        inv_freq = 1.0 / torch.pow(10000, torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float().div(dim))
        angles = torch.outer(positions, inv_freq)
        self.register_buffer("cos", angles.cos().repeat_interleave(2, dim=1), persistent=False)
        self.register_buffer("sin", angles.sin().repeat_interleave(2, dim=1), persistent=False)

    def forward(self, x):
        cos = self.cos.to(x.device)[None, :, None, :]
        sin = self.sin.to(x.device)[None, :, None, :]
        x_real, x_imag = x.float().reshape(*x.shape[:-1], -1, 2).unbind(-1)
        x_rotated = torch.stack([-x_imag, x_real], dim=-1).flatten(3)
        return (x.float() * cos + x_rotated * sin).to(x.dtype)


def run_aot(model_cls, device):
    model = model_cls().to(device).eval()
    x = torch.randn(1, 8, 2, 16, device=device)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        package_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, f"{model_cls.__name__}.pt2")
        exported = torch.export.export(model, args=(x,))
        torch._inductor.aoti_compile_and_package(exported, package_path=package_path)
        loaded = load_package(package_path, run_single_threaded=True)
        return loaded(x)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="xpu", choices=["xpu", "cuda", "cpu"])
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.device == "xpu" and not (hasattr(torch, "xpu") and torch.xpu.is_available()):
        raise RuntimeError("XPU is not available")
    if args.device == "cuda" and not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA is not available")

    print(f"torch={torch.__version__}")
    print(f"torch.version.cuda={torch.version.cuda}")
    print(f"torch.version.xpu={getattr(torch.version, 'xpu', None)}")
    print(f"device={args.device}")

    for model_cls in (ComplexRope, RealRope):
        print(f"\n=== {model_cls.__name__} ===")
        try:
            out = run_aot(model_cls, args.device)
            print(f"PASS shape={tuple(out.shape)} device={out.device} dtype={out.dtype}")
        except Exception as error:
            print(f"FAIL {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
            traceback.print_exc(limit=8)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## Actual Result

```text
torch=2.13.0.dev20260519+xpu
torch.version.cuda=None
torch.version.xpu=20250302
device=xpu

=== ComplexRope ===
FAIL RuntimeError: AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled

=== RealRope ===
PASS shape=(1, 8, 2, 16) device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32
```

Relevant error excerpt:

```text
Error: aoti_torch_proxy_executor_call_function(... std::array<AtenTensorHandle, 2>{_tensor_constant0, buf3}.data()) API call failed
RuntimeError: AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled
```

In another run with a related larger model, the same class of failure also surfaced through XPU AOT shim calls such as:

```text
aoti_torch_xpu_slice_Tensor ... API call failed
strides() called on an undefined Tensor
```

## Expected Result

`ComplexRope` should either compile and run successfully on XPU through AOTInductor package, or fail with a clear unsupported-complex-operator diagnostic that does not appear as a CUDA initialization/assertion error.

Since `RealRope` is mathematically equivalent and passes through the same AOT package flow, this appears isolated to the complex tensor implementation path rather than the general XPU device or AOT package setup.

## Notes

The failing operation pattern is common in RoPE implementations:

```python
freqs = torch.polar(torch.ones_like(angles), angles)
x_complex = torch.view_as_complex(x.float().reshape(*x.shape[:-1], -1, 2))
out = torch.view_as_real(x_complex * freqs.to(x.device).unsqueeze(1)).flatten(3)
```

A workaround is to rewrite RoPE using real-valued `cos/sin` tensors:

```python
out = x * cos + rotate_half(x) * sin
```

That workaround passes in this repro, but it would be useful to know whether complex RoPE-style computations are expected to be supported by XPU AOTInductor package, and if so, whether this CUDA assertion is a bug in the fallback/proxy execution path.

```bash
### Standalone repro, proves the bug is in `at::native::xpu::max_pool2d_with_indices_backward_kernel` (no inductor, no triton involvement):


import torch
aten = torch.ops.aten

def fn(a, b, c):
    return aten.max_pool2d_with_indices_backward(
        a, b, [13, 13], [1, 1], [2, 2], [1, 1], False, c
    )

torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn([2, 64, 20, 20])
result, indices = aten.max_pool2d_with_indices(x, [13, 13], [1, 1], 2, 1, False)
grad_fp32 = torch.randn_like(result)

ref_fp32 = fn(grad_fp32, x, indices)
ref_fp16 = ref_fp32.to(torch.float16).to("xpu")

eager_fp16 = fn(
    grad_fp32.to("xpu").to(torch.float16),
    x.to("xpu").to(torch.float16),
    indices.to("xpu"),
)

inductor_fp16 = torch.compile(fn, fullgraph=True)(
    grad_fp32.to("xpu").to(torch.float16),
    x.to("xpu").to(torch.float16),
    indices.to("xpu"),
)

for name, out in [("eager_fp16_vs_ref", eager_fp16), ("inductor_fp16_vs_ref", inductor_fp16)]:
    diff = (ref_fp16.float() - out.float()).abs()
    n = (diff > 1e-5).sum().item()
    print(f"{name}: mismatched={n}/{out.numel()}, max_abs={diff.max().item()}")

diff_e_i = (eager_fp16.float() - inductor_fp16.float()).abs()
print(f"eager_fp16_vs_inductor_fp16: mismatched={(diff_e_i > 1e-5).sum().item()}/{eager_fp16.numel()}, max_abs={diff_e_i.max().item()}")

title: Improve errors logging when run_test_with_skip.py is executed

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

When tests are executed stderr is redirected to a file *_test_error.log. But it is not shown in console so GitHub will not saved them. Also because two separate files are created *_test_error.log and *_test.log without any timestamps there is no possibility to see what test cause what error or what happened during each test execution. This is not a problem when the same error is captured by python and show in test summary but that's no the case for some tests. Also if test is random sometime is hard to reproduce a problem but if occur on CI, it will be a great addition to debugging if there is a log error with additional information.

```
python run_test_with_skip.py \
          2> ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test_error.log | \
          tee ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test.log
```

### Alternatives

1) First fix is to just save all the data in one file. So redirect 2>&1. Main log file for Linux op_ut is ~83MB so adding an error log ~180KB is not a big problem in terms of log size.
2) Second idea is to leave two separate logs but use for both of them tee and redirect stderr to console to have all needed data in one GitHub log.

```
python run_test_with_skip.py \
          > >(tee ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test.log) \
          2> >(tee ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test_error.log >&2)
```

title: [BMG][oneAPI 2026.0.0] 18 confirmed Dynamo perf drops < 0.90x on Battlemage

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Summary

During oneAPI 2026.0.0 validation on BMG (Intel Arc Pro B60), 18 model/dtype/mode combinations show confirmed inductor performance drops below the 0.90× threshold after rerun-merge (best-of-2 runs).

## Key Affected Models

| Model | Ind Ratio | Dtypes/Modes |
|-------|---------------|--------------|
| `pyhpc_turbulent_kinetic_energy` | 0.673–0.822× | float32/float16/amp_fp16/bfloat16/amp_bf16 inference (5 cases) |
| `AlbertForMaskedLM` | 0.770–0.871× | amp_bf16/amp_fp16 training (2 cases) |
| `AllenaiLongformerBase` | 0.826–0.836× | bfloat16/float16 inference (2 cases) |
| `pytorch_unet` | 0.866–0.869× | bfloat16/amp_bf16/float16/amp_fp16 inference (4 cases) |
| `GPT2ForSequenceClassification` | 0.895–0.899× | amp_bf16/amp_fp16/bfloat16/float16 training (4 cases) |
| `squeezenet1_1` | 0.899× | amp_bf16 inference (1 case) |

## Methodology

Each (suite, dtype, mode, model) was measured in two independent GH Actions runs. The **best** (higher) inductor ratio is reported. After rerun-merge, 18 cases remain < 0.90 (down from 26 first-run drops). 8 first-run drops recovered above 0.90.

## Context

- These regressions are introduced by the oneAPI 2025.3.2 → 2026.0.0 runtime swap.
- Hardware, GPU driver, kernel, container OS, Python, and Triton are identical across both runs.
- The overall inductor geomean is still **1.020×** (net positive), but these specific models regress.
- `pyhpc_turbulent_kinetic_energy` is the worst (0.67× on float32), suggesting a possible kernel-generation or code-selection issue in the new SYCL runtime for that specific workload.

## Reproducer

```
docker run -it -e TZ=Aisa/Shanghai --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --privileged --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-24.04-rolling:26.05 bash

# setup python
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | env UV_INSTALL_DIR="/usr/local/bin" sh
uv venv myvenv --python 3.10 --clear
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip numpy 'setuptools<81' wheel

# get wheel built with 2026.0.0
gh --repo pytorch/pytorch run download 25343551532 -p "manywheel-py3_10-xpu"
pip install manywheel-py3_10-xpu/torch-*.whl --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/xpu

# prepare pytorch
pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch
cd ${PYTORCH_DIR}
git reset --hard
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

# install deps
uv pip install pip pandas psutil scipy requests
uv pip install -U numpy==1.26.4
uv pip install transformers==4.55.2 accelerate
uv pip install timm==1.0.19

title: Improve random label behavior

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

As it is now the random label prevent from closing issue when it pass. But also preventing from inserting comment with pass message so after adding random to issue there is no update from CI when issue pass or fail. Which in some cases is problematic as issue reproduce in specific condition.

### Alternatives

Add new check to ut_result_check.sh script to insert comment with information if test cases from issue marked as random fail or pass. This will give us clear history of nightly runs and also we will be able quickly check how often the problem occur.

### Additional context

I had issue: https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/issues/3195 marked as random and I was not able to find single nightly run that fail but I also don't check every run. Only fail is a pull request run. So with such nightly history I will be able to quickly tell if the test fail again.

title: [kernel][perf]index_select / embedding kernel 5-22x slower on XPU vs CUDA
body:
`torch.index_select` (used internally by `torch.nn.functional.embedding`) is 5-22x slower on XPU compared to CUDA for identical workloads. Non-contiguous index tensors exacerbate the gap (~2.7x additional penalty on XPU vs ~1.2x on CUDA).

This was discovered during roofline projection analysis of 154 OOB models. `aten::embedding` has R_op ≈ 0.01 in models like LayoutLMForMaskedLM, making it the second-largest projection deficit across the fleet.

reproducer:
 python repro_embedding.py --device xpu
```
import argparse, time, torch

def benchmark(weight_shape, indices_shape, stride_mode, device, warmup=20, repeat=50):
    vocab_size, embed_dim = weight_shape
    weight = torch.randn(vocab_size, embed_dim, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)

    if stride_mode == "contiguous":
        indices = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, indices_shape, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    else:
        flat = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (indices_shape[0] * 2048,), dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        indices = torch.as_strided(flat, indices_shape, (2048, 4))

    sync = torch.cuda.synchronize if device == "cuda" else torch.xpu.synchronize

    for _ in range(warmup):
        torch.index_select(weight, 0, indices.reshape(-1))
    sync()

    times = []
    for _ in range(repeat):
        sync()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        torch.index_select(weight, 0, indices.reshape(-1))
        sync()
        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)

    return sorted(times)[len(times) // 2]
if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cuda", choices=["cuda", "xpu"])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    d = args.device

    cases = [
        ("Large vocab, contiguous",    (30522, 768), (128, 512), "contiguous"),
        ("Small vocab, non-contiguous", (1024, 768),  (128, 512), "non-contiguous"),
        ("Small vocab, contiguous",     (1024, 768),  (128, 512), "contiguous"),
        ("Tiny vocab, contiguous",      (2, 768),     (128, 512), "contiguous"),
    ]

    print(f"Device: {d} ({torch.xpu.get_device_name(0) if d == 'xpu' else torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)})")
    print(f"PyTorch: {torch.__version__}\n")
    for name, ws, ids, stride in cases:
        ms = benchmark(ws, ids, stride, d)
        print(f"  {name:>35} | {ms:.3f} ms")
```

CUDA dispatches to `vectorized_gather_kernel` (contiguous) or `_scatter_gather_elementwise_kernel` (non-contiguous). XPU uses `at::native::xpu::IndexKernel` for all cases.

Model Impact:
In full-model profiling (LayoutLMForMaskedLM_bs128), embedding calls account for 239ms of GPU time on B580 vs 1.3ms on 4080S.

body:
## Bug Description

`test_get_device_properties_tensor_device` fails because `torch._C._XpuDeviceProperties` does not have `max_threads_per_multi_processor` attribute. The test was ported from CUDA where `CudaDeviceProperties` has this attribute.

## Affected Tests

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.dynamo.test_functions_xpu.FunctionTests,test_get_device_properties_tensor_device

## Error Message

```
AttributeError: 'torch._C._XpuDeviceProperties' object has no attribute 'max_threads_per_multi_processor'
```

## Context

Surfaced by PR #3383 (CI run 25534217826) which ported `test_functions_xpu.py`.

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

New failing test cases appeared in the latest Nightly / Build-from-source and in some pull workflows:
https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/actions/runs/25439279276

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_ops_xpu.TestOperatorsXPU,test_vjpvmap_nn_functional_conv3d_xpu_float32

### Likely root cause

Many similar test cases related to convolution operations that call oneDNN kernels under the hood are failing due to default non deterministic behavior of the oneDNN kernels. That causes slightly different results between consecutive kernel launches with exactly the same inputs, which makes the tests fail as they expect more exact results.
Quick test if that is the root cause is to launch the same tests with `DeterministicGuard(True)` context manager that changes oneDNN kernels into deterministic mode.

title: [XPU] Enable functionalize_rng_ops on XPU (philox_rand prim + RNG decompositions)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

test_cases:
  - test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout
  - test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout_inductor
---

## Parent Issue

Follow-up to intel/torch-xpu-ops#1970 — *RuntimeError: CUDA not available from CUDARngStateHelper*.

The PyTorch in-tree fix for #1970 makes `CUDARngStateHelper` device-agnostic via
`torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()` (alias preserved). With that change, the
two reporting tests get past `CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple` but now
hit a **second, deeper layer of CUDA-only gates** in the AOTAutograd
`functionalize_rng_ops=True` path. Enabling those tests on XPU requires generalizing
that path. This issue tracks that work.

## Affected Test Cases

After the helper fix and `device=GPU_TYPE` retargeting:

- `test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout`
- `test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout_inductor`

Same root cause is expected to surface in any other test that toggles
`torch._functorch.config.functionalize_rng_ops=True` and runs on a non-CUDA accelerator.

## Root Cause

The functionalized-RNG lowering for `aten.rand` / `aten.rand_like` / dropout is
currently CUDA-only at three places:

1. **`torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py`** — `rand` (line 33) and `rand_like`
   (line 56) explicitly call `throw_on_non_cuda(device)` for any non-CUDA device.
2. **`torch/_prims/rng_prims.py`** — `_philox_rand` impl (line 116) raises
   `throw_on_non_cuda` when `device.type != "cuda"`.
3. **`torch/_prims/rng_prims.py:philox_rand_offset`** (line 71) — hardcodes
   `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(torch.cuda.current_device())` and reads
   `multi_processor_count` / `max_threads_per_multi_processor`. These fields do not
   exist on `torch.xpu.get_device_properties()` (XPU exposes `gpu_eu_count`,
   `max_compute_units`, `gpu_subslice_count`, `max_num_sub_groups`,
   `max_work_group_size` instead).

Functionally, XPU already uses Philox/counter-based RNG (`torch.xpu.initial_seed`,
`_get_rng_state_offset`, `_set_rng_state_offset`, `set_rng_state` exist and have
the same semantics as the CUDA equivalents), so generalization is feasible — only
the device-properties query and the hard gates are CUDA-shaped.

## Reproducer

After applying intel/torch-xpu-ops#1970's fix
(`CUDARngStateHelper` → `RngStateHelper`) and switching the two tests to
`device=GPU_TYPE` + `@requires_gpu_and_triton`:

```bash
cd <pytorch>
python test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py \
    ActivationCheckpointingTests.test_dropout \
    ActivationCheckpointingTests.test_dropout_inductor
```

Fails with:

```
RuntimeError: You are trying to functionalize a xpu RNG operator but xpu does not
use Philox/counter-based RNG. Therefore, functionalizing a xpu RNG operator is not
supported. ...
```

raised from `torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py:23`.

## Scope of Changes

### Files to update (PyTorch in-tree)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py` | Replace `throw_on_non_cuda` gate in `rand` / `rand_like` with an "accelerator supports Philox" check (allow `cuda`, `xpu`, future Philox-capable backends). Update message accordingly. |
| `torch/_prims/rng_prims.py` (`_philox_rand` impl) | Drop the `device.type != "cuda"` raise; route `set_torch_state_tensor` through the device-agnostic `RngStateHelper` (already done by #1970 follow-up); call `torch.rand(shape, device=device, ...)` which already works on XPU. |
| `torch/_prims/rng_prims.py` (`philox_rand_offset`) | Generalize the device-properties query. Introduce a small helper `_philox_offset_grid_params(device)` that returns `(block_size, blocks_per_sm, sm_count)`-equivalent values per backend. For XPU, derive from `max_compute_units`, `max_work_group_size`, `gpu_subslice_count`, `max_num_sub_groups`. A safe alternative is a conservative upper-bound offset jump that does not depend on hardware geometry — acceptable because over-advancing the Philox counter only wastes counter space, not correctness. |
| `torch/_prims_common/__init__.py` | Already done by #1970 follow-up (`RngStateHelper` device-agnostic). No further change. |

### Out of scope (do separately)

- Numerical equivalence of the XPU Philox stream vs. eager XPU RNG output.
  `philox_rand` is a *new* RNG stream tracked by AOTAutograd; it is not required
  to match the existing eager `torch.rand` numerics on XPU. The two existing
  tests use `skip_check=True` for this exact reason.
- Inductor lowering of `philox_rand` for the XPU backend. `aot_eager` should
  work after the in-tree fix; `inductor` may need a separate Triton/SYCL lowering
  if a kernel-level emit is missing. Verify before scoping.
- Other accelerators (`hpu`, `mps`). Pattern should be extensible but not part
  of this issue.

### Suggested approach

1. Introduce a backend predicate (`_supports_philox_functionalization(device)`)
   and use it in both `decompositions_for_rng.py` and `rng_prims.py`. Initial
   set: `{"cuda", "xpu"}`.
2. Generalize `philox_rand_offset` to accept `device` (already in the signature
   via callers — currently ignored) and dispatch device-properties lookup off
   `device.type`. For XPU, use:
   - `block_size`: `max_work_group_size` (typically 1024).
   - `sm_count`-equivalent: `gpu_subslice_count` or `max_compute_units / threads_per_eu`.
   - Or take the conservative path and compute a safe upper-bound offset jump
     independent of geometry.
3. Route `_philox_rand`'s `set_torch_state_tensor` call through the
   device-agnostic `RngStateHelper` (no API change — it already resolves the
   active accelerator after #1970 fix).
4. Extend the `test_dropout` / `test_dropout_inductor` enablement to verify
   both `aot_eager` and `inductor` paths on XPU.

### Test plan

- Re-run the two `ActivationCheckpointingTests` on XPU; both must pass.
- Add a smoke test in `test/test_prims.py` that exercises
  `torch.ops.rngprims.philox_rand` directly on the active accelerator.
- Sanity-check CUDA path is unaffected by re-running
  `test/test_prims.py` and one CUDA-pinned `test_dropout*` variant if available.

## Representative Error

```
File "/home/tszulist/src/pytorch/torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py", line 56, in rand_like
    throw_on_non_cuda(device)
File "/home/tszulist/src/pytorch/torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py", line 23, in throw_on_non_cuda
    raise RuntimeError(
torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='compiler_fn' raised:
RuntimeError: You are trying to functionalize a xpu RNG operator but xpu does
not use Philox/counter-based RNG. Therefore, functionalizing a xpu RNG operator
is not supported. We are discussing the possibility of a Philox-based RNG
implementation for CPU.
```

## Shared Context

- HW: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100 (and BMG); reproduces on any XPU host.
- Software: PyTorch `main` after #1970's `CUDARngStateHelper` fix.
- Dependency on #1970: this issue is only meaningful **after** #1970's helper
  generalization is merged. Without it, the failure surfaces earlier (in
  `_prims_common`) and masks the deeper gates this issue addresses.
- Where the PR belongs: PyTorch in-tree (`pytorch/pytorch`), not `torch-xpu-ops`.
- Labels suggested: `module: xpu`, `module: functorch`, `module: dynamo`.

title: [split from #3093] NestedTensor SDPA on XPU has no viable backend (jagged path)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

test_cases:
  - op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_nestedtensor_xpu.TestNestedTensorSubclassXPU,test_sdpa_with_packed_in_proj_xpu_bfloat16
---

## Parent Issue

Split from #3093 — XPU does not support NestedTensor for SDPA operations.

## Affected Test Cases

- `test_nestedtensor_xpu.py::TestNestedTensorSubclassXPU::test_sdpa_with_packed_in_proj_xpu_bfloat16`

(The closely-related `test_dummy_mha_with_nt_use_legacy_api_{True,False}_xpu` cases mentioned in the parent issue are already skipped on XPU since torch-xpu-ops commit `7625ae9b` via `@skipXPUIf(True, "XPU does not support NestedTensor for SDPA operations.")`. They no longer reproduce.)

## Root Cause

`F.scaled_dot_product_attention` on jagged-NestedTensor inputs is dispatched to `jagged_scaled_dot_product_attention` in `torch/nested/_internal/sdpa.py`, which calls `_select_sdp_backend` (line 293). On XPU all four candidate backends are rejected:

| Backend | Why it fails on XPU |
|---|---|
| `CUDNN_ATTENTION` | `torch._C._can_use_cudnn_attention` is guarded `#ifdef USE_CUDA` only in `torch/csrc/Module.cpp` (always returns `False` on XPU). |
| `FLASH_ATTENTION` | `aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/xpu/sdp_utils.cpp::can_use_flash_attention` includes `check_nested_tensor` (in `sdp_utils_cpp.h`), which unconditionally rejects nested inputs. CUDA's version splits constraints into a separate nested branch and accepts them. |
| `EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` | `torch._C._can_use_mem_efficient_attention` is guarded `#ifdef USE_CUDA` only. |
| `MATH` | This specific test produces non-contiguous q/k/v (`# these are non-contiguous to trigger _is_safe_to_get_storage_as_tensor()`); `_can_use_math_sdpa_jagged` rejects them via the `transpose(1,2).is_contiguous()` check. |

The test does **not** wrap the call in any `sdpa_kernel(...)` context, so the failure mode here differs from the vmap `backend3` cases (sub-issue 1): math is enabled but rejected by the contiguity check, not by user-disabling.

Even when `_can_use_math_sdpa_jagged` accepts inputs, the broader gap remains: XPU has no XPU-specific `_flash_attention_forward` (CUDA-only dispatch in `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml`), no efficient/cuDNN attention, and no jagged constraint relaxation. The in-flight work pytorch/pytorch#180857 + intel/torch-xpu-ops#3405 (blocked on intel/torch-xpu-ops#3140) is intended to add an XPU varlen flash kernel and the jagged-NT plumbing.

## Reproducer

```bash
cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
python -m pytest -sxv test_nestedtensor_xpu.py \
  -k "test_sdpa_with_packed_in_proj_xpu_bfloat16"
```

## Representative Error

```
W0430 08:28:17.712000 sdpa.py:327] Memory efficient kernel not used because:
W0430 08:28:17.713000 sdpa.py:330] Flash attention kernel not used because:
W0430 08:28:17.713000 sdpa.py:333] Math attention kernel not used because:
W0430 08:28:17.713000 sdpa.py:280] If inputs are nested tensors they must be contiguous after transposing.
W0430 08:28:17.713000 sdpa.py:335] cuDNN attention kernel not used because:
.../test_nestedtensor_xpu.py:7193: UserWarning: Both fused kernels of cpp version currently do not support Nested Tensor inputs. (Triggered internally at .../aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/sdp_utils_cpp.h:230.)
  output = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None)
FAILED

=================================== FAILURES ===================================
____ TestNestedTensorSubclassXPU.test_sdpa_with_packed_in_proj_xpu_bfloat16 ____
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../test/xpu/test_nestedtensor_xpu.py", line 7193, in test_sdpa_with_packed_in_proj
    output = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None)
  File ".../torch/nested/_internal/nested_tensor.py", line 396, in __torch_function__
    return jagged_torch_function(func, *args, **kwargs)
  File ".../torch/nested/_internal/ops.py", line 390, in jagged_torch_function
    return jagged_scaled_dot_product_attention(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../torch/nested/_internal/sdpa.py", line 934, in jagged_scaled_dot_product_attention
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: No viable backend for scaled_dot_product_attention was found.
```

## Recommended Fix Direction

- **Short term**: add `@skipXPUIf(True, "XPU does not support NestedTensor for SDPA operations.")` to `test_sdpa_with_packed_in_proj` (mirroring the existing decorator on `test_dummy_mha_with_nt`).
- **Long term**: rely on pytorch/pytorch#180857 + intel/torch-xpu-ops#3405 to land XPU varlen FlashAttention, then either drop `check_nested_tensor` from XPU `can_use_flash_attention` and add an XPU dispatch entry for `_flash_attention_forward`, or implement an `OVERRIDEABLE` SDPA backend selector for XPU.

## Shared Context

- Reproduced 2026-04-30 on `pytorch` HEAD (current branch `main`) with `torch-xpu-ops` pinned at `d67a87783002c17786e9501c8c67b360479f6bb7`.

title: [split from #3093] vmap SDPA tests parametrize CUDNN_ATTENTION (backend3) on XPU which has no cuDNN backend

labels.name: skipped
labels.description: Used for temp UT failure to parallel fix

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

test_cases:
  - op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_vmap_xpu.TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU,test_randomness_backend3_randomness_different_xpu
  - op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_vmap_xpu.TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU,test_randomness_backend3_randomness_error_xpu
  - op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_vmap_xpu.TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU,test_randomness_backend3_randomness_same_xpu
  - op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_vmap_xpu.TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU,test_sdpa_backend3_xpu
---

## Parent Issue

Split from #3093 — XPU does not support NestedTensor for SDPA operations.

## Affected Test Cases

- `test_vmap_xpu.py::TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU::test_randomness_backend3_randomness_different_xpu`
- `test_vmap_xpu.py::TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU::test_randomness_backend3_randomness_error_xpu`
- `test_vmap_xpu.py::TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU::test_randomness_backend3_randomness_same_xpu`
- `test_vmap_xpu.py::TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU::test_sdpa_backend3_xpu`

## Root Cause

These four tests are parametrized over the `PLATFORM_SPECIFIC_SDPA` backend list at the top of `test/xpu/functorch/test_vmap_xpu.py`. Lines 109-110 unconditionally append `SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION` for XPU:

```python
# For XPU, add CUDNN_ATTENTION even though it's not supported - tests will fail with known issue
if TEST_XPU and SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION not in PLATFORM_SPECIFIC_SDPA:
    PLATFORM_SPECIFIC_SDPA.append(SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION)
```

This makes the `backend3` parametrization point at `SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION`. Each test wraps its SDPA call in `sdpa_kernel([backend])`, so all other backends (FLASH/EFFICIENT/MATH/OVERRIDEABLE) are disabled. XPU has no `_cudnn_attention_forward` registration (Python hook `torch._C._can_use_cudnn_attention` is `#ifdef USE_CUDA`-only in `torch/csrc/Module.cpp`), so the dispatcher rejects every backend and raises:

> RuntimeError: No viable backend for scaled_dot_product_attention was found. This is likely due to turning off both the math kernel and the overrideable kernels.

Inputs in these tests are **dense** tensors, so the failure happens in the C++ dense SDPA selector (not in `jagged_scaled_dot_product_attention`). The "overrideable" kernel hook is also not enabled for XPU SDPA in this code path.

This is a **test-side defect**: XPU should not advertise `CUDNN_ATTENTION` as a supported backend. The author of those lines was aware (`"# … tests will fail with known issue"`), but the test was not actually skipped for the cuDNN parametrization.

## Reproducer

```bash
cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/functorch
PYTHONPATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/test/functorch:$PYTHONPATH \
  python -m pytest -sxv test_vmap_xpu.py \
  -k "test_randomness_backend3_randomness_different_xpu or \
      test_randomness_backend3_randomness_error_xpu or \
      test_randomness_backend3_randomness_same_xpu or \
      test_sdpa_backend3_xpu"
```

(`PYTHONPATH` is needed so `from common_utils import …` at the top of `test_vmap_xpu.py` resolves to `pytorch/test/functorch/common_utils.py`.)

## Representative Error

```
test_vmap_xpu.py::TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU::test_randomness_backend3_randomness_different_xpu FAILED
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
_ TestVmapBatchedGradientXPU.test_randomness_backend3_randomness_different_xpu _
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../test/xpu/functorch/test_vmap_xpu.py", line 3970, in test_randomness
    vmap(
  File ".../torch/_functorch/apis.py", line 220, in wrapped
    return vmap_impl(
  File ".../torch/_functorch/vmap.py", line 316, in vmap_impl
    return _flat_vmap(
  File ".../torch/_functorch/vmap.py", line 507, in _flat_vmap
    batched_outputs = func(*batched_inputs, **kwargs)
  File ".../test/xpu/functorch/test_vmap_xpu.py", line 3967, in f
    return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, dropout_p=dropout)
RuntimeError: No viable backend for scaled_dot_product_attention was found. This is likely due to turning off both the math kernel and the overrideable kernels.
```

## Recommended Fix Direction

- Either remove the unconditional `CUDNN_ATTENTION` append for XPU at `test_vmap_xpu.py:109-110`, or skip the `_backend3_*` parametrization for XPU (e.g. with `@skipXPUIf(True, "no cuDNN backend on XPU")` on `test_randomness` and `test_sdpa`, or by adding `_backend3_` to the `skip_list_common.py` entry — note the file is currently `None`-skipped there but the `op_ut` runner used to reproduce bypasses that).
- This is independent of the NestedTensor flash work in pytorch/pytorch#180857 and intel/torch-xpu-ops#3405; even after those land, XPU still has no cuDNN attention.

## Shared Context

- Reproduced 2026-04-30 on `pytorch` HEAD (current branch `main`) with `torch-xpu-ops` pinned at `d67a87783002c17786e9501c8c67b360479f6bb7` (file `third_party/xpu.txt`).

title: [Bug Skip] XPU index_add_ numerical accuracy: 3 test_index_add_correctness_2d_* cases (bf16, fp32+alpha)

labels.name: skipped
labels.description: Used for temp UT failure to parallel fix

body:
## Bug Description

`torch.Tensor.index_add_` (and the out-of-place equivalent) on XPU produces
numerically inaccurate results when used with `bfloat16` and with `float32 +
non-default alpha`, exceeding the tolerances upstream's `test_indexing.py`
applies. Three cases under `TestIndexingXPU` fail:

## Affected Tests

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_indexing_xpu.TestIndexingXPU,test_index_add_correctness_2d_alpha_xpu
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_indexing_xpu.TestIndexingXPU,test_index_add_correctness_2d_large_xpu_bfloat16
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_indexing_xpu.TestIndexingXPU,test_index_add_correctness_2d_out_of_place_xpu_bfloat16

## Error Messages

### `test_index_add_correctness_2d_alpha_xpu` (float32 + alpha)

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 37 / 3200 (1.2%)
Greatest absolute difference: 9.012222290039062e-05 at index (58, 13)
Greatest relative difference: 0.0005161699373275042 at index (58, 13)
File ".../test/test_indexing.py:2218"
    self.assertEqual(dst.cpu(), dst_ref, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
```

### `test_index_add_correctness_2d_large_xpu_bfloat16`

```
AssertionError: 0.016779609101716046 not less than 0.01 :
    index_add_ torch.bfloat16 L2 rel err too high: 0.016779609101716046
File ".../test/test_indexing.py:2158"
```

### `test_index_add_correctness_2d_out_of_place_xpu_bfloat16`

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 52 / 6400 (0.8%)
Greatest absolute difference: 0.28363037109375 at index (38, 10)
Greatest relative difference: 0.4216286838054657 at index (177, 27)
File ".../test/test_indexing.py:2198"
    self.assertEqual(out_func.cpu().float(), ref, atol=atol, rtol=rtol)
```

## Reproduction

```bash
cd $HOME/daisy_pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
pytest -v test_indexing_xpu.py::TestIndexingXPU::test_index_add_correctness_2d_alpha_xpu
pytest -v test_indexing_xpu.py::TestIndexingXPU::test_index_add_correctness_2d_large_xpu_bfloat16
pytest -v test_indexing_xpu.py::TestIndexingXPU::test_index_add_correctness_2d_out_of_place_xpu_bfloat16
```

## Root Cause Analysis

All three failures point at the XPU `index_add_` kernel:

- The `_alpha` variant uses fp32 inputs and a non-trivial `alpha` scalar; the
  observed error (~9e-5 abs, ~5e-4 rel) exceeds upstream's tight
  `atol=rtol=1e-5`. Likely a non-deterministic-or-different-order
  reduction in the XPU kernel.
- Both `_bfloat16` variants are large 2-D tests where bf16 precision combined
  with kernel reduction order produces L2 relative error of ~0.017–0.42,
  well above the bf16-specific tolerances upstream has tuned for CUDA
  (`L2_rel < 0.01`, and per-element `atol/rtol` tighter than 0.05).

This is consistent with XPU `index_add_` using a different parallel
reduction layout than CUDA, accumulating in lower precision than CUDA's
fp32 accumulator path.

## Context

This issue tracks an XPU numerical-accuracy gap surfaced (but not introduced)
by PR [#3475](https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/pull/3475). PR #3475
enables broader test coverage on XPU; `test_indexing_xpu.py` already exists
on `main`, and these three `test_index_add_correctness_2d_*` cases were
already failing prior to PR #3475 — they appear unfiltered in the PR's
`linux-ut (op_ut) / summary` artifact because no existing tracking issue
covers them.

For PR #3475 to land green, this issue must be `skipped`-labeled with the
`Cases:` lines above so the `ut_result_check.sh` filter stops flagging them
as new failures.

PR: https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/pull/3475

## Versions

PyTorch: 2.13.0.dev (April 2026 nightly)
Hardware: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100/1550

## Labels

- `skipped`
- `module: ut`
- `module: nn`

body:
## Bug Description

Five upstream `test_multiprocessing.py::TestMultiprocessing` cases fail on XPU
when run via the XPU-port wrapper `test/xpu/test_multiprocessing_xpu.py`.
Failures cover three distinct underlying gaps but are tracked as one issue
because they all live in the same ported test class and the dynamic-skip
mechanism filters by `Cases:` lines. Filing them together keeps `Cases:`
line drift to a minimum.

## Affected Tests

Cases:
~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_multiprocessing_xpu.TestMultiprocessing,test_is_shared_cuda~~
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_multiprocessing_xpu.TestMultiprocessing,test_integer_parameter_serialization_cpu
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_multiprocessing_xpu.TestMultiprocessing,test_meta_simple
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_multiprocessing_xpu.TestMultiprocessing,test_autograd_fine_with_spawn
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_multiprocessing_xpu.TestMultiprocessing,test_cuda_bad_call

## Sub-failures and root causes

### 1. `test_is_shared_cuda`

The PR overrides this test with `_test_is_shared_xpu` which asserts that
`torch.randn(5, 5).xpu().is_shared()` returns `True`. On CUDA, GPU tensors
are auto-shared (CUDA IPC semantics); XPU does not auto-share fresh tensors.

```
AssertionError: False is not true
File "test_multiprocessing_xpu.py", line 82
    self.assertTrue(t.is_shared())
```

XPU semantics may legitimately differ from CUDA here (no IPC by default).
Either the assertion needs adjusting to XPU behaviour or XPU needs to mark
device tensors shared after `.xpu()` (matching CUDA).

### 2. `test_integer_parameter_serialization_cpu`

Upstream test, runs `_test_integer_parameter_serialization(device="cpu")`.
The CPU-device variant fails:

```
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!
Expected 1 but got 0.
Failed to serialize successfully for "cpu" device!
File ".../test/test_multiprocessing.py:1015"
```

This appears unrelated to XPU but surfaces in the XPU port because the
wrapper imports the upstream class wholesale. Likely a flaky multiprocessing
serialization race; needs investigation to confirm.

### 3. `test_meta_simple`

```
File ".../test/test_multiprocessing.py:343, in test_fill"
    self.assertTrue(is_set)
AssertionError: False is not true
```

Spawned worker fails to set the `is_set` event when sharing a meta tensor.
Possibly a timing/race condition with `mp.get_context("spawn")` on this
hardware; CUDA path apparently passes.

### 4. `test_autograd_fine_with_spawn`

```
worker 'gw9' crashed while running
'.../test_multiprocessing_xpu.py::TestMultiprocessing::test_autograd_fine_with_spawn'
```

xdist worker crash, no usable traceback. Flaky; reproduces under op_ut's
load.

### 5. `test_cuda_bad_call`

PR overrides this test with `_test_cuda_bad_call`, but the body still
relies on `queue_get_exception` which does `torch.zeros(5, 5).cuda()`
in the child. On a non-CUDA build, `.cuda()` raises
`AssertionError("Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled")`, not
`RuntimeError`, breaking the assertion:

```
AssertionError: AssertionError('Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled')
                is not an instance of <class 'RuntimeError'>
```

The CUDA-specific re-init semantics this test verifies have no clean XPU
analog with the existing `queue_get_exception` helper. The override either
needs to use a different child function (calling `.xpu()` from a
fork-after-init context) or the test should be skipped on XPU as
CUDA-specific.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd $HOME/daisy_pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
pytest -v test_multiprocessing_xpu.py::TestMultiprocessing::test_is_shared_cuda
pytest -v test_multiprocessing_xpu.py::TestMultiprocessing::test_integer_parameter_serialization_cpu
pytest -v test_multiprocessing_xpu.py::TestMultiprocessing::test_meta_simple
pytest -v test_multiprocessing_xpu.py::TestMultiprocessing::test_autograd_fine_with_spawn
pytest -v test_multiprocessing_xpu.py::TestMultiprocessing::test_cuda_bad_call
```

## Context

This issue tracks gaps identified during PR
[#3475](https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/pull/3475), which enables
broad CUDA test coverage on XPU including `test_multiprocessing_xpu.py`.

In that PR, the five cases listed under **Affected Tests** are currently
**enabled-but-failing** on XPU. Once the underlying gaps (XPU `is_shared`
semantics, `_test_cuda_bad_call` XPU-equivalent helper, multiprocessing
flakiness) are resolved, the dynamic-skip entries that PR #3475 adds via
this issue's `Cases:` lines can be removed and the tests will pass without
further code changes.

PR: https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/pull/3475

## Versions

PyTorch: 2.13.0.dev (April 2026 nightly)
Hardware: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100/1550

## Labels

- `skipped`
- `module: ut`

# [PyTorch CI] DISABLED test_max_reads_limits_fusion (OverFusionTest) on XPU

**Labels:** `pytorch-ci-failure`

---

### Failure Type

`NEW_FAILURE`

---

### Commit Scope

The test `test_max_reads_limits_fusion` was introduced by pytorch/pytorch#179494
(merged Apr 21 2026, commit `300d114e2fd`) and immediately fails on XPU CI.
No prior passing run exists for this test on XPU.

| Status | Commit | Note |
|--------|--------|------|
| ➕ Test introduced | `300d114e2fd` | [inductor] Fix mix_order_reduction over-fusion via load count check |
| ❌ Disabled on XPU | — | pytorch/pytorch#181699 |

Upstream issue: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/181699

---

### Failed Tests

- `test/inductor/test_mix_order_reduction.py::OverFusionTest::test_max_reads_limits_fusion`

---

### Error Log

```
# Full error log not yet captured — test is DISABLED upstream before a log was recorded.
# Likely failure modes (from code analysis):
#
# Candidate 1 — numerical mismatch in bfloat16 backward pass on XPU:
#   AssertionError: False is not true
#   (self.assertTrue(same(grad_ref, grad_act, tol=5e-2)) fails for XPU bfloat16)
#
# Candidate 2 — metric assertion: mix_order_reduction not triggered on XPU:
#   AssertionError: 0 not greater than 0
#   (self.assertGreater(metrics.codegen_mix_order_reduction, 0))
#
# Candidate 3 — metric assertion: max_reads rejection not triggered on XPU:
#   AssertionError: 0 not greater than 0
#   (self.assertGreater(metrics.rejected_mix_order_reduction_fusion, 0))
```

---

### CI Job URL

https://torch-ci.com/failure?failureCaptures=%5B%22test%2Finductor%2Ftest_mix_order_reduction.py%3A%3AOverFusionTest%3A%3Atest_max_reads_limits_fusion%22%5D

---

### Repro Commands

```bash
# From pytorch/pytorch root with XPU environment sourced
source ~/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh
source .venv/bin/activate

python test/inductor/test_mix_order_reduction.py \
    OverFusionTest.test_max_reads_limits_fusion \
    2>&1 | tail -60
```

---

### Background

The test was added in pytorch/pytorch#179494 to verify that `triton.mix_order_reduction_max_reads`
limits over-fusion in transformer backward passes. The fix introduced
`FusedMixOrderReductions.can_fuse_with` logic in `torch/_inductor/scheduler.py:2268`
that counts `tl.load()` reads and rejects fusion when the count exceeds `max_reads`.

On XPU, `GPU_TYPE = "xpu"` and `HAS_GPU = True` (via `HAS_XPU_AND_TRITON`), so the
test is not skipped by the `if not HAS_GPU` guard. The XPU backend does implement
`codegen_mix_order_reduction` via `XPUCombinedScheduling`
(`torch/_inductor/codegen/xpu/xpu_combined_scheduling.py:97`), which delegates to
`_triton_scheduling`. However, the test uses a 3-layer GQA + QK-norm model in
`bfloat16` whose backward numerical accuracy or kernel fusion behaviour on XPU may
diverge from the CUDA baseline expectations.

---

- [ ] Reproduce on XPU dev machine
- [ ] Identify root cause (numerical / metric / codegen)
- [ ] Implement fix or add XPU-specific tolerance/skip
- [ ] Verify fix locally
- [ ] PR proposal
- [ ] Human review
- [ ] PR creation

# Issue Creation for CI Failure - PR Split & Validation Plan

**Last Updated:** 2026-04-29
**Target Repo:** intel/torch-xpu-ops
**Tracking Issue:** #3503

---

## Design Principles

1. **Label:** `pytorch-ci-failure` - distinguishes PyTorch mainline CI failures from torch-xpu-ops internal issues
2. **Title Prefix:** `[PyTorch CI]`
3. **Classification Strategy:**
   - **Summary issue:** factual - NEW_FAILURE / EXISTING_FAILURE (pure data comparison between runs)
   - **Sub-issues:**  Creating sub-issues would result in a multi-issue list and could cause the number of issues to explode, so this will not be automated for now.
4. **Schedule Control:** repo variable `CI_MONITOR_ENABLED` (true/false) gates cron triggers; `workflow_dispatch` always available

---

## Pipeline Overview

```
Step 1: Scan CI (PR2 - MERGED)
  Input:  GitHub API (PyTorch XPU workflow runs)
  Output: ci_results.json, all_runs.json (uploaded as artifact)

Step 2: Create Summary Issue (PR3)
  Input:  ci_results.json, all_runs.json
  Output: GitHub issue with commit scope, NEW/EXISTING classification

Step 3: Workflow Integration (PR3)
  Input:  All scripts from Step 1-3
  Output: Updated ci_break_monitor.yml with all steps wired together

Create Sub-Issues (will not be automated for now and manually trigger with local script)
  Input:  ci_results.json, summary issue number
  Output: One sub-issue per test-file group
```

---

## PR Details

### PR 1: Issue Template - MERGED (#3507 )

**Files:**
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ci-failure-tracking.yml`

### PR 2: CI Scanner Script + Workflow - MERGED (#3525)

**Files:**
- `.github/scripts/check_nightly_status.py`
- `.github/workflows/ci_break_monitor.yml`

**Key features:**
- Scan PyTorch XPU CI workflow runs via GitHub API
- Deep-scan EXISTING failures to find first-fail commit scope
- File-path based workflow ID lookup with name-based fallback
- Auth header leak prevention on log download redirects
- Non-success conclusion coverage (not just failure/timed_out)
- `pull_request` trigger with path filters for CI validation

### PR 3: Issue Creation + Sub-Issue Classification + Workflow Integration (IN PROGRESS)

**Files:**

- `.github/scripts/classify_failures.py` - Create sub-issues per test-file group

**What PR3 does (combined from original PR3/4/5):**

1. **create_tracking_issue.py** (Step 2):
   - Reads ci_results.json + all_runs.json from Step 1
   - Computes commit scope (last PASS -> first FAIL) from push runs timeline
   - Finds suspect commits within scope via Compare API
   - Creates/updates a GitHub issue with structured failure report
   - Supports `--dry-run` for local testing
   - Outputs `issue_number` for downstream steps

2. **classify_failures.py** (Step 3):
   - Reads ci_results.json + summary issue number from Step 2

   - Closes sub-issues for tests that are now fixed
   - Supports `--dry-run` for local testing

3. **Workflow updates** (Step 4):
   - Adds Step 2 (create tracking issue) and Step 3 (classify failures) to ci_break_monitor.yml
   - Adds `issues: write` permission for issue creation
   - Updates `pull_request.paths` to include new scripts
   - All step `if` conditions cover `schedule`, `pull_request`, and `workflow_dispatch`

**Validation:**

2. PR trigger runs full pipeline on GitHub Actions
3. Verify issue creation on torch-xpu-ops with correct format

title: [release/2.12] PT2E INT8 performance regression on resnext50_32x4d (XPU): ~12% Asymm / ~13% Symm slower on 2.12.0+xpu vs release/2.11
body:
### Summary
On `torch==2.12.0+xpu`, PT2E (inductor) INT8 throughput on XPU regresses ~12–13% on `resnext50_32x4d` versus `release/2.11`, while FP32 throughput is unchanged. Both `XPU_QUANT_CONFIG=ASYMM` and `XPU_QUANT_CONFIG=SYMM` are affected, so this is not config-specific — it points at the shared INT8 (oneDNN graph) lowering / kernel selection on XPU.

### Environment
- `torch`: `2.12.0+xpu` (target) vs `release/2.11` (baseline)
- Device: XPU
- Benchmark harness: `https://github.com/zxd1997066/benchmark` branch `yifeng/pt2e_xpu` cloned as `pt2e-performance`
- Mode: eval, channels-last, `--torchdynamo inductor`, PT2E quantization

### Reproduce
```bash
git clone -b yifeng/pt2e_xpu https://github.com/zxd1997066/benchmark pt2e-performance

PERF_CMD="python pt2e-performance/run_benchmark.py xpu \
          --test eval --channels-last --metrics throughputs --torchdynamo inductor"
m=resnext50_32x4d

# FP32 (unchanged)
${PERF_CMD} -m "${m}"

# INT8 ASYMM (regressed)
XPU_QUANT_CONFIG=ASYMM ${PERF_CMD} -m "${m}" --quantization pt2e

# INT8 SYMM (regressed)
XPU_QUANT_CONFIG=SYMM  ${PERF_CMD} -m "${m}" --quantization pt2e
```
Throughput is parsed from `pt2e-performance/.userbenchmark/**/eval_throughput`.

### Results

`resnext50_32x4d` throughput (eval, channels-last, inductor):

| Mode       |  target / baseline |
|------------|-----------------:|
| FP32       |             1.003 |
| Asymm INT8 |              **0.884** |
| Symm INT8  |            **0.868** |

→ INT8 regression **−11.6% (Asymm)** and **−13.2% (Symm)**; FP32 within noise.

### Analysis (PyTorch + torch-xpu-ops code refs)

The PT2E INT8 path on XPU goes through the shared mkldnn lowerings and dispatches to oneDNN graph extern kernels:

1. **Quantized-conv lowering is shared CPU/XPU** — `torch/_inductor/mkldnn_ir.py` (`QConvPointWisePT2E.create` → `_prepare_convolution_fusion_create`), gated by `SUPPORTED_MKLDNN_DEVICES = ("cpu", "xpu")` in `torch/_inductor/utils.py`. The XPU side resolves to `aoti_torch_xpu__qconv_pointwise_tensor`. Any change to the shared lowering between 2.11 and 2.12 (channels-last propagation, weight reorder, post-op fusion choice) directly affects XPU throughput.

2. **Algorithm selection for extern quantized kernels** — `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py` around L3254 catches `TensorMeta.from_irnodes(...)` failures for the extern choice. If meta is missing on XPU, the autotuner cannot benchmark variants and may fall back to a non-optimal kernel — which would manifest as a perf regression even when accuracy survives.

3. **Weight zero-point materialization** — `torch/_inductor/mkldnn_lowerings.py` near L763 wraps `w_zp` via `torch.tensor(w_zp_tensor, dtype=torch.int32)`. The same regression footprint appearing under both ASYMM and SYMM suggests the perf hit is not in the asymmetric-only zero-point branch but in the common reorder/fusion path.

4. **`resnext50_32x4d` is grouped-conv heavy (cardinality=32)**. Grouped INT8 convolution on XPU is the most layout/format-sensitive path in oneDNN graph; a change in channels-last propagation or grouped-conv fusion eligibility would land here first. The fact that FP32 is unchanged and INT8 is regressed for both quant configs strongly localizes the regression to the INT8 conv lowering / fusion / kernel selection — not to dataloader, dynamo tracing, or post-grad passes.

### Likely root-cause hypotheses (ranked)
1. **Grouped INT8 conv fusion / channels-last propagation regression** in the shared `_prepare_convolution_fusion_create` path between 2.11 → 2.12 (selecting a slower oneDNN primitive or losing post-op fusion on grouped conv).
2. **Extern-choice autotuner degradation on XPU** due to `TensorMeta.from_irnodes` failures (`select_algorithm.py` L3254) leading to suboptimal kernel selection for `qconv_pointwise`.
3. **Weight reorder regression** for INT8 grouped weights on XPU (the `w_zp` rewrap path in `mkldnn_lowerings.py` near L763 indicates the constant-materialization branch is exercised every run).

### Related
- Accuracy regression (likely same lowering area): intel/torch-xpu-ops#3489

title: [release/2.12] PT2E INT8 accuracy regression on shufflenet_v2_x1_0 (XPU): Acc@1 66.5 → 0.09 between release/2.11 and 2.12.0+xpu
body:
### Summary
On `torch==2.12.0+xpu`, PT2E (inductor) INT8 quantization of `shufflenet_v2_x1_0` on XPU collapses to near-random accuracy. The same flow on `release/2.11` reaches Acc@1 66.5 / Acc@5 86.528, and FP32 on the same 2.12.0+xpu build is healthy. This is a regression in the XPU PT2E INT8 path.

### Environment
- `torch`: `2.12.0+xpu`
- Python 3.12 (venv at `/workspace/myvenv`)
- Device: XPU
- Quant config: default, PT2E flow via `pt2e-accuracy/scripts/modelbench/quant/inductor_quant_acc.py`
- Dataset: ImageNet ILSVRC2012 val (standard valprep)

### Reproduce
```bash

git clone -b main https://github.com/chuanqi129/inductor-tools pt2e-accuracy

ACC_CMD="python pt2e-accuracy/scripts/modelbench/quant/inductor_quant_acc.py \
         --device xpu --dataset_dir ${DATASET_DIR}"
m=shufflenet_v2_x1_0

# INT8 (broken on 2.12.0+xpu)
${ACC_CMD} --model_list "${m}"

# FP32 (healthy, sanity check)
${ACC_CMD} --model_list "${m}" --is_fp32
```

### Results

| Build | Mode | Acc@1 | Acc@5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| release/2.11 | INT8 (default config) | **66.500** | **86.528** |
| 2.12.0+xpu | INT8 (default config) | **0.090** | **0.482** |
| 2.12.0+xpu | FP32 | 69.356 | 88.314 |

### Observed log (INT8 run, 2.12.0+xpu, abridged)
```
using ptq
W0427 05:36:24 torch/_inductor/codecache.py:832] [1/0] pre_grad_custom_pass function does not implement uuid(); falling back to early timing ...
/workspace/myvenv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_inductor/mkldnn_lowerings.py:763: UserWarning:
  To copy construct from a tensor, it is recommended to use sourceTensor.detach().clone() ...
  torch.tensor(w_zp_tensor, dtype=torch.int32), name=w_zp.get_name()
W0427 05:36:28 torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:3254] [1/0] Constructing input/output tensor meta failed for Extern Choice

shufflenet_v2_x1_0 int8:  * Acc@1 0.090 Acc@5 0.482
```

(The two `torchao` `_C_mxfp8.so` / `_C_cutlass_90a.abi3.so` "Failed to load" lines at startup are unrelated CUDA-only artifacts shipped in the wheel.)

### Analysis (PyTorch + torch-xpu-ops code refs)

The two warnings emitted only on the INT8 path point at the inductor PT2E lowering for XPU, which is shared with CPU via the mkldnn lowerings:

1. **Weight zero-point handling** — `torch/_inductor/mkldnn_lowerings.py` around L763, in the QConv/QLinear PT2E lowering:
   ```python
   w_zp_tensor = V.graph.constants[w_zp.get_name()].to(torch.int32)
   w_zp = V.graph.add_tensor_constant(
       torch.tensor(w_zp_tensor, dtype=torch.int32),  # <-- triggers the warning
       name=w_zp.get_name(),
   )
   ```
   The `torch.tensor(<existing tensor>, dtype=int32)` re-wrap is what produces the user-warning, and is the canonical path for `w_zp` on the PT2E flow. A dtype/layout mismatch here would directly corrupt weight quantization math.

2. **Extern-kernel meta construction failure** — `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py` around L3254:
   ```python
   try:
       self.input_tensor_meta  = TensorMeta.from_irnodes(self.input_nodes)
       self.output_tensor_meta = TensorMeta.from_irnodes(self.layout)
   except Exception:
       log.warning("Constructing input/output tensor meta failed for Extern Choice")
   ```
   On XPU this exception is being swallowed for the quantized extern choice, so algorithm selection proceeds with empty meta and an extern fallback may be picked / dispatched with the wrong layout. This warning does **not** appear on the FP32 run.

3. **`QConvPointWisePT2E` is shared CPU/XPU** — `torch/_inductor/mkldnn_ir.py` (`QConvPointWisePT2E.create` → `_prepare_convolution_fusion_create`, gated by `SUPPORTED_MKLDNN_DEVICES = ("cpu", "xpu")` in `torch/_inductor/utils.py`). The XPU side delegates to oneDNN graph via the kernel name `aoti_torch_xpu__qconv_pointwise_tensor`. Any change in the shared lowering between 2.11 and 2.12 (w_zp dtype/stride, channels-last propagation, grouped-conv handling) would land on XPU even if originally targeted at CPU.

`shufflenet_v2_x1_0` is depthwise/grouped-conv heavy and uses channel-shuffle, which historically has been the most fragile shape for INT8 conv lowerings — consistent with this being the first model to fail.

### Likely root-cause hypotheses (ranked)
1. **Weight zero-point dtype/layout regression** in the shared mkldnn PT2E lowering (`mkldnn_lowerings.py` near L763) — the warning is emitted on every INT8 run.
2. **Extern-choice TensorMeta failure on XPU** (`select_algorithm.py` L3254) leading to wrong kernel selection for `qconv_pointwise` on XPU.
3. **Grouped/depthwise INT8 lowering gap on XPU** in `_prepare_convolution_fusion_create` (`mkldnn_ir.py`) — would explain why shufflenet is hit first.

title: [Bug Skip] test_philox_rand on XPU: CUDARngStateHelper has no XPU equivalent

labels.name: skipped
labels.description: Used for temp UT failure to parallel fix

body:
## Bug Description

`test_prims.test_philox_rand` is collected for the XPU device via `test_prims_xpu.py` but fails because the test body unconditionally calls `CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple()`, which raises `RuntimeError: CUDA not available` on XPU-only machines. The upstream test is decorated `@onlyCUDA`, but the XPU port file (or the `XPUPatchForImport` pre-import shim) re-routes it to XPU and the body itself remains CUDA-hardcoded.

## Affected Tests

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_prims_xpu.TestPrimsXPU,test_philox_rand_xpu_float32

## Error Message

```
RuntimeError: CUDA not available
```

## Test Code Snippet

```python
# pytorch/test/test_prims.py:281-310 (test_philox_rand)
@onlyCUDA
@dtypes(torch.float32)
def test_philox_rand(self, device, dtype):
    sizes = (1000, 1000000)
    repeats = 2
    for size in sizes:
        torch.cuda.manual_seed(123)
        references = []
        results = []
        rng_states = []
        for _ in range(repeats):
            rng_states.append(CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple())  # FAILS here on XPU
            ...
```

```python
# pytorch/torch/_prims_common/__init__.py: CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple
@staticmethod
def get_torch_state_as_tuple(fake_mode=nullcontext()):
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA not available")
    ...
```

## Traceback

```
pytest_command:
cd ~/daisy_pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
pytest -v test_prims_xpu.py -k test_philox_rand_xpu_float32

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../test/test_prims.py", line 286, in test_philox_rand
    rng_states.append(CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple())
  File ".../torch/_prims_common/__init__.py", line 2198, in get_torch_state_as_tuple
    raise RuntimeError("CUDA not available")
RuntimeError: CUDA not available
```

## Root Cause Analysis

Two factors combine:

1. The XPU port re-routes `test_philox_rand` to the XPU device despite the upstream `@onlyCUDA` decorator — likely because `XPUPatchForImport` neutralises `@onlyCUDA` so the test body is dispatched on XPU.
2. The test body is CUDA-specific by construction: it uses `CUDARngStateHelper`, which gates on `torch.cuda.is_available()`. There is no XPU equivalent of `CUDARngStateHelper` exposed by `torch._prims_common`.

This is therefore a coverage gap, not a numeric bug:
- Either the XPU port should keep the `@onlyCUDA` decorator effective and skip the test on XPU, or
- An XPU equivalent of `CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple()` (e.g. `XPURngStateHelper`) should be added so the test can be ported faithfully and exercise XPU's philox RNG path.

## Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

- (none found for `philox` on XPU as of 2026-04-25)

## Versions

- pytorch: source build (HEAD)
- torch-xpu-ops: HEAD
- env: pytorch_opencode_env on PVC
